abstract.para: The Apache HTTP Server (Apache) is a feature-rich, open source Web server. The Apache HTTP Server Project maintains stable release branches and follows a compatibility-oriented release policy. These upstream compatibility principles, together with SUSE's package lifecycle policies, inform the update and maintenance strategy for Apache packages in &suselinux; &productnumber;.

topic.para: In &suselinux; &productnumber;, Apache follows the stable lifecycle model. This model balances the delivery of security fixes and other relevant upstream changes with the compatibility and long-term stability expected from SUSE Linux Enterprise systems.

section.title: Upstream compatibility policy
section.para: The Apache HTTP Server Project follows a stable-release policy designed to preserve compatibility between revisions of a stable branch.

listitem.para: Stable branch: Apache uses even-numbered minor versions to identify stable branches.

Forward compatibility: Revisions within a stable branch are intended to retain forward compatibility to the maximum possible extent. Features may be added during revisions, and features may be deprecated with appropriate documentation.
Module API: The Apache module API is designed to retain forward compatibility between revisions of a stable branch.
Runtime configuration: The runtime configuration is designed to remain forward-compatible between revisions of a stable branch.

Compile-time configuration: The compile-time configuration is designed to remain forward-compatible. The configure command-line options supported by one revision of a stable branch are intended to remain supported by subsequent revisions.

note.para: The compatibility policy described above is an Apache HTTP Server upstream policy. It does not constitute an unconditional compatibility guarantee for every third-party module, local customization or deployment configuration. Verify new Apache package versions with their particular configuration and module set before deploying updates in production.

section.title: Update strategy and lifecycle model
section.para: For Apache in &suselinux; &productnumber;, SUSE maintains the stable update strategy, which combines a rolling-style update approach during General Availability (GA) with a more conservative approach during LTS.

listitem.para: For &suselinux; minor releases in GA, the Apache package is upgraded when a new upstream Apache version is released. New upstream versions are typically released several times per year.

When a &suselinux; minor release enters LTS, the Apache version is frozen. Version upgrades are avoided during LTS unless they are considered necessary. Potential version upgrades are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, taking into account security, maintenance and compatibility requirements.

section.para: The LTS freeze does not prevent an exceptional version update when one is required. In particular, SUSE retains the option of performing an emergency version update when necessary to address a critical security vulnerability or other exceptional requirement.
